question.text:
What is $X$ in the following reaction?
$\mathrm{CO}+2 \mathrm{H}_2 \xrightarrow{x} \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{OH}$

solution.text: The given reaction is for the industrial preparation methanol from a mixture of carbon monoxide and hydrogen . In the reaction the gaseous mixture is subjected to 200 atmosphere and then passed over heated catalyst mixture of ZnO and $\mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O}_3$ kept at $573-673 \mathrm{~K}$. This reaction results the formation of methanol vopours which are then condensed to liquid state.

question.text: An unknown alochol is treated with the "Lucas reagent" to determine whether the alcohol is primary, secondary or tertiary. Which alcohol reacts fastest and by what mechanism :

solution.text: The reaction of alcohol with Lucas reagent is mostly an $\mathrm{S}_{N}1$ mechanism reaction and the rate of reaction is directly proportional to the carbocation stability formed in the reaction, hence tertiary alcohol will react fastest.

Which of the following is/are aromatic alcohol?

solution.text:
The aromatic alcohols are those compounds in which the hydroxyl group is not directly attached to the nucleus but is linked to a carbon atom situated in a side-chain.

The compound-I and compound-II are the phenols, these are not the aromatic alcohols as -OH group is directly attached to benzene ring.

The compounds II and III are benzyl alcohols and these are aromatic alcohols as -OH group is attached to the carbon atom which itself attached to benzene ring.
